title: Early-commit prefill and jittered burst mitigation for vector API
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce p95/p99 tail at the embeddings (vector) endpoint caused by short-lived bursts and KV-prefill stalls. Approach combines an early-commit prefill path, jittered ingress throttling (burst smoothing), and a small kernel-level hotpatch to avoid a synchronous cold KV load on critical codepaths. We expect to recover ~30-55% of tail latency in mixed traffic without materially affecting throughput or median latency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) p99 for 1-4KB embeddings under mixed tenant traffic drops >= 30% in staging vs baseline; 2) no regression in p50/p95 more than 5%; 3) integration tests for prefill fast-path + fallback exercised; 4) telemetry exposed: prefill-hit-rate, jittered-drop-rate, kernel-fallback-count
notes_and_tradeoffs:
- Trade-offs: early-commit prefill increases memory pressure for short-lived KV allocations; to limit cost we bound prefill to the first 8 requests per tenant per 10s window.
- We avoid full speculative warmup for very large contexts due to GPU time waste; large-context requests keep existing path.
- Kernel hotpatch is minimal (guarded hop to async prefetch) to reduce risk; this requires careful rollout with circuit breaker.
implementation_plan: 1) Add prefill fast-path in ingress: detect small embedding requests and issue async KV prefill while returning a lightweight placeholder to scheduler; 2) Implement jittered ingress shaper that spreads bursts over 50-200ms windows using exponential jitter; 3) Add kernel hook to attempt non-blocking KV async fetch with synchronous fallback; 4) Add telemetry and alerting (p99-sla, prefill-fallback-rate); 5) Canary (5% traffic) -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error budgets
telemetry_baseline: staging baseline p50=28ms, p95=210ms, p99=720ms for 256-dim vectors under synthetic mixed-tenant burst; prefill hit-rate=0% (no prefill), observed KV-sync stalls present in flamegraphs at ingress+kernel boundary
staging_results: proof-of-concept run 2025-02-25: p50=30ms, p95=180ms, p99=410ms (43% p99 improvement) with prefill bound=8 and jitter window=100ms. Prefill-hit-rate=67%, kernel-fallback-rate=3%. Memory transient increase ~6% on canary host. Need longer run for stability
risks: Increased memory pressure on high-churn tenants
Potential regression for large-batch throughput if prefill heuristics trigger incorrectly
Kernel hotpatch may expose rare race - requires fuzz testing
mitigations: Bound prefill by tenant/window and total inflight prefill budget per host
Add automatic disable flag in console to turn off prefill per-tenant
Rollout with circuit breaker and extended canary with synthetic burst tests
